feeling: A carefully kept lane feels reassuring until something moves behind the hedge.
arrival: Straight hedge edges and white lamps frame clean paving, while rounded tree crowns hide the ground beyond.
art: Keep the regular formal setts, clipped hedge row and white lamps just off the road.
Use rounded crowns on detected trees within three cells; keep the ground free of grass tufts.
Let the existing hedge art conceal the ambush approach without obscuring the road.

mechanics.text: A hedge ambush can emerge from behind the first verge row.
Walking the route restores its paving.
Give the occupied hedge a brief rustle before the ambush activates, so an attentive walker can prepare.

loop: Enjoy the order, notice the rustle, clear the ambush, continue restoring.

feeling: Walking the road feels like moving through the life of a forest.
arrival: Tiny seedlings give way to young pines, mature crowns, bare trunks and stumps, with a shrine beyond the last group.
art: Keep one verge row with one empty cell between specimens and clearly distinct growth stages.
Use the existing pine, dead-tree and stump art; omit shrubs and extra tree rows.
Keep grass sparse and low so the sequence and final shrine remain readable.

mechanics.text: The generated row follows the growth-to-stump sequence and seats its shrine after the stumps.
Plant guards and a wild-boar encounter interrupt the woodland walk; some streets also have a bear.
Make the final shrine visibly brighten when the whole local sequence has been walked, using restoration progress as the trigger.

loop: Follow the tree sequence, deal with wildlife, reach the shrine.

feeling: Food within reach makes the lane inviting, but harvesting asks the player to lower their guard.
arrival: Fruit catches the eye among rounded crowns immediately beside the road, with a farmer goblin farther along the row.
art: Keep fruit trees and mature maples in the first verge row, with blocked seats left empty.
Make apples readable through foliage; reserve orange and Worldpeach colors for occasional trees.
Keep the current soft pink lamp glow restrained so it does not compete with the fruit colors.

mechanics.text: The lane supplies fruit trees, mostly apples with occasional oranges and Worldpeaches.
Farmer-goblin guards make some harvesting stops contested.
Use a brief fruit sparkle on harvestable trees, disappearing after collection, to make a worthwhile stop readable while walking.

loop: Spot ripe fruit, check for a guard, harvest, move to the next tree.

feeling: A quiet passage becomes a short, deliberate route-planning puzzle.
arrival: A few smooth stones sit at uneven distances from the road, and the first lights when stepped on.
art: Scatter the existing waystones across both two-cell verges instead of making a tidy border.
Keep churchyard ground, restrained conifers and pale lamps visually subdued.
Give active waystone glow enough contrast to read against the old stone ground.

mechanics.text: Step on the three to six waystones before their lights fade to complete the set.
The completed set records its reward, so the same puzzle cannot be farmed repeatedly.
Let active stones pulse faster as their remaining time runs low, communicating urgency without another timer panel.

loop: Read the scattered layout, choose an order, keep every stone lit.

feeling: The route feels like a continuous chain of small refuges after darker stretches.
arrival: Closely spaced amber lamps lead the eye ahead before any other roadside object does.
art: Use the existing dense lantern spacing and warm amber light as the main identity.
Keep paving and rounded trees muted so lamp silhouettes remain distinct.
Use the shipping lamp art consistently; avoid adding unrelated decorative props between every post.

mechanics.text: Lamps are placed more densely than on ordinary routes.
Walking restores the route through the shared street-restoration system.
Give each newly restored lamp a short warm ignition pulse, making forward progress visible down the chain.

loop: Follow the lights and leave a visibly restored trail behind.

feeling: Every unnecessary pause feels costly on a road that is still burning.
arrival: Orange seams glow between black stones, with tar, stakes and a fire-slime guard interrupting the way ahead.
art: Preserve the ember cracks in dark paving so danger reads from the ground itself.
Use bare trees, scorched debris and sparse red-orange lights.
Keep ember brightness separate from ordinary lantern glow so the damaging surface is unmistakable.

mechanics.text: The hot road damages grounded players through the shared hazard system.
Tar, stakes and a fire-slime guard create obstacles along the stretch.
Place a small visibly cool rest pocket at each end, giving players a clear place to prepare and recover before crossing.

loop: Prepare on safe ground, cross decisively, deal with the guard, recover beyond the heat.

feeling: The road feels occupied, and opening it becomes a small act of reclamation.
arrival: Upright torch flames reveal wooden barriers across the route, with scattered stakes in the broad dirt verges.
art: Use upright open-flame torch posts, rough timber barriers and iron stakes.
Keep dirt three cells deep and scatter rocks and planks without creating neat rows.
Use bare trees and subdued paving so barriers and gaps remain the clearest shapes.

mechanics.text: Barricades cross the route and extend into its verges; goblins guard the area.
A Trap Kit removes individual barrier pieces.
Give the final piece blocking a continuous passage a distinct break sound and brief dust burst, marking the moment the road opens.

loop: Assess the blockage, clear the defenders, open a passage.

feeling: The lane invites curious foraging while making every large clump a possible hiding place.
arrival: Small caps lead toward thicker mushroom clumps and an occasional giant, with warm light catching their spots.
art: Use the approved mushroom replacements 02→01 and 09→07.
Keep small pickups common, medium clumps clearly bush-sized, and giants occasional.
Retain damp ground and orange lamps; separate mushroom silhouettes from the rounded tree canopy.

mechanics.text: Small mushrooms can be collected; medium mushroom bushes use bush chopping and cover.
Spider guards make dense fungal patches worth checking before entering.
Let disturbed medium clumps shed a brief harmless spore puff, making harvesting and an approaching creature readable through the cover.

loop: Collect small caps, inspect the cover, chop a clump or skirt the danger.

feeling: The open water makes continuing along the path feel rewarding in itself.
arrival: The land opens on one side, and warm paving leads along the visible shoreline toward a vista.
art: Keep the water-facing edge open and reserve conifers for the landward side.
Use sandy-gold paving and warm lamps against the existing water art.
Place the vista chest where the shore remains visible rather than hiding it behind decorative clutter.

mechanics.text: Qualifying shoreline stretches grant double first-restoration credit.
Eligible scenic stretches can place a one-time vista chest.
Use a subtle glint from the vista chest when it first enters view, encouraging a short shoreward detour without a quest marker.

loop: Follow the shoreline, restore new ground, step aside for the vista reward.

feeling: A living corridor makes the player want to slow down and watch the verge.
arrival: Low branches frame the path, and a deer appears between the rounded crowns and grass.
art: Use rounded mossy trees and low hanging canopy shapes already in the theme.
Keep deer silhouettes visible through gaps rather than burying them in dense ground cover.
Use restrained green lamps and small grass patches without introducing shoreline scenery.

mechanics.text: Deer are seeded along qualifying greenway paths.
Scenic greenway stretches grant increased first-restoration credit and can hold a one-time vista chest.
Let nearby deer briefly look toward a slow or stationary player before resuming their existing behavior, rewarding attention without another collectible.

loop: Follow the green corridor, notice wildlife, continue toward the next opening.

feeling: Small signs of former care make this path feel worth bringing back.
arrival: Old paving remains visible beneath weeds and leaves, with a soft lamp marking the next bend.
art: Keep the existing park ground, rounded shade trees and restrained green-white lamps.
Concentrate leaves and weeds at paving edges so the route remains legible.
Use the current white-flower accents sparingly to suggest a surviving garden rather than dense wild forest.

mechanics.text: Qualifying park paths grant increased first-restoration credit.
Eligible scenic stretches can place a one-time vista chest.
Fade the leaf-and-weed edge clutter back locally as paving is restored, giving this route a clear before-and-after payoff with existing art.

loop: Follow the neglected path and watch its shape return as you walk.

feeling: A lucky discovery becomes a small daily ritual.
arrival: The gilded shrine draws you off the ordinary road before the reward appears.
art: Use the original Golden Road story art to introduce the shrine.
Keep the gilded shrine brighter than the muted stone and ordinary lamps.
Leave both coin rows visually clear of decorative clutter.

mechanics.text: Touching the shrine starts a daily green-coin run along both road verges.
The themed section is capped at 250 m.
Briefly pulse the first available coins after activation so the collection route reads immediately.

loop: Notice shrine → activate → sweep both verges → return another day.

feeling: Temptation makes every next step a deliberate choice.
arrival: A visible chest promises a reward while open iron jaws interrupt the approach.
art: Frame the existing chest with readable iron-trap silhouettes.
Keep bones, rocks and broken planks lower contrast than armed traps.
Use the original Snare Lane story art to establish the risk before the player approaches.

mechanics.text: A chest is surrounded by a trap cluster, with additional snares along road and verges.
Scattered bones, rocks and planks occupy the three-cell dusty verge.
Highlight the nearest armed trap on approach without revealing traps elsewhere.

loop: Spot cache → inspect approach → avoid or handle traps → claim chest.

feeling: The route feels neglected and resistant to passage.
arrival: Bramble clusters break the road rhythm; a partly hidden cairn offers a reason to push through.
art: Use existing brambles as solid silhouettes against dry khaki ground.
Give the moss cairn a clear focal point inside its compact thorn ring.
Keep loose roadside thorns distinct from harmless dead-tree branches.

mechanics.text: Bramble clusters cross the road and extend into its three-cell verges.
Brambles drain energy on contact and can burn; some streets enclose a moss cairn.
Give brambles a brief contact shake to distinguish their damage from nearby enemies.

loop: Read thorn gaps → choose passage or clearance → reach cairn → continue.

feeling: You have walked into someone else’s territory.
arrival: Barrel stacks and grouped goblins signal occupied ground rather than an isolated encounter.
art: Make existing barrel stacks the landmark for each gang.
Keep goblin silhouettes visible around the stacks.
Use dusty ground and plank fragments to connect each group without adding new fortifications.

mechanics.text: Up to six gang clusters occupy a section where space permits.
Each cluster combines goblin guards with up to five barrels.
Add a short shared alert gesture when one gang notices the player.

loop: Spot gang → choose engagement or bypass → inspect barrels → assess next group.

feeling: A narrow trail invites an easy, satisfying reward run.
arrival: An end shrine promises a line to follow rather than a wide area to search.
art: Retain the original Golden Path story art and gilded shrine.
Use existing paired candles as a quiet edge cue.
Keep the green coins legible along the path centre.

mechanics.text: Either end shrine activates the same daily coin run.
Coins appear along the path centreline.
Show a brief directional glint down the coin line after activation.

loop: Touch either shrine → follow centreline coins → leave at the far end.

feeling: The trail feels inhabited by a persistent, sticky colony.
arrival: Wet green ground and familiar slime shapes announce a continuous enemy territory.
art: Use the current slime-pattern pavement accent to connect encounters.
Show the section’s chosen slime species consistently.
Keep wet slicks distinct from walkable stone and enemy bodies.

mechanics.text: Each section selects one slime species from its configured pool.
Eligible posts hold two guards about 70 m apart; short sections use a midpoint post.
Let cleared posts briefly lose their strongest slime shimmer so progress feels visible.

loop: Recognize species → approach pair → fight or bypass → read next colony post.

feeling: Forward movement becomes fragile: a careless step can hold you in danger.
arrival: Pale silk interrupts the dark path while spiders wait nearby.
art: Keep existing pale webs high contrast against cave-floor ground.
Use dead-tree silhouettes and bone fragments to frame, not obscure, silk.
Retain original Spider Path story art rather than adding giant decorative spiders.

mechanics.text: Lasting webs occupy 35% of eligible samples and paralyse grounded actors.
A section has one two-spider garrison.
Add a short silk-tension animation when a web catches an actor.

loop: Identify webs → choose clear footing → manage spiders → cross the section.

feeling: The air itself makes lingering feel costly.
arrival: Green vent clouds draw attention to pockets of danger around a damp path.
art: Use existing poison vent animation and green gas as the primary warning.
Separate the toad-idol shrine silhouette from green orb lamps.
Keep wet ground darker than the gas so its extent stays readable.

mechanics.text: Poison vents erupt beside the route and emit poison gas.
The daily shrine grants eight minutes of Mending regeneration, not poison immunity.
Strengthen the vent warning pulse at the edge of the visible screen.

loop: Watch vent cycle → avoid gas → visit shrine if useful → move onward.

feeling: Crossing feels like timing a dangerous opening.
arrival: Flame vents and warm lamps reveal a scorched route with intermittent danger.
art: Use upright flame lamps as steady lights and vent animation as the changing hazard.
Preserve dark rocks and dead-tree art around orange flames.
Give the ember altar a distinct silhouette from ordinary fire fixtures.

mechanics.text: Fire vents warn, erupt, apply burning and leave temporary ground fire.
The daily ember shrine strengthens magic for five minutes; it does not grant fire immunity.
Make the last warning beat visually sharper before eruption.

loop: Observe warning → cross a safe interval → avoid lingering fire → consider altar.

feeling: Stopping in the wrong place can cost control of the encounter.
arrival: Vent warnings compete with creeping tendrils along the roadside.
art: Use existing paralysis vent frames against muted stone.
Keep creeping-vine tendrils visibly separate from lavender-tree foliage.
Frame the bone-watcher shrine with a clear approach rather than hiding it in vines.

mechanics.text: Paralysis gas can prevent movement and attacks.
A creeping-vine colony grows from a roadside seed; tendrils sting on contact.
Make safe gaps between vines and vent footprints easier to read with restrained edge contrast.

loop: Read vents and vines → choose a clear crossing → avoid becoming trapped → reach watcher if useful.

feeling: A familiar path becomes briefly hard to trust.
arrival: Violet vapour and lavender trees suggest disorientation while lamps remain landmarks.
art: Use the existing confusion gas and lavender-tree art together.
Keep green orb lamps visually steady against moving vapour.
Distinguish the lantern-saint shrine from luminous mushroom bulbs and dark urns.

mechanics.text: Confusion vents release gas that disrupts steering.
The daily lantern shrine boosts light for five minutes; it does not cure confusion.
Keep a subtle stable path-edge cue visible through the effect to aid reorientation.

loop: Read vapour → avoid exposure → regain bearings if affected → follow the route out.

feeling: An inviting food stop becomes a lesson in watching the bushes.
arrival: Ordinary bushes and fruiting bushes close around both verges, with occasional thorns breaking the soft outline.
art: Use the existing plain, fruiting and poison-berry bush silhouettes; keep plain bushes dominant.
Keep thorns sparse and omit yellow flowers so fruit and movement remain the strongest signals.
Use the existing warm lamp glow to reveal gaps between bushes.

mechanics.text: Harvest berry bushes; picked fruit leaves the bush standing, while poison and golden berries retain their existing effects.
Goblin runts can lurk behind the bush row; brambles punish careless contact.
Give a concealed runt a brief foliage rustle before its first approach, rewarding a pause before harvesting.

loop: Notice fruit → inspect cover → harvest or skirt the bushes → continue.

feeling: Abundant food feels claimed by something larger than you.
arrival: Fruit-heavy bushes crowd the narrow trail, and a large bear occupies the same stretch.
art: Use denser existing berry-bush art than Berry Lane, with a few poison bushes and brambles.
Keep the bear readable through breaks in the bushes rather than adding new scenery.
Retain the narrow path silhouette so approaching the fruit feels like a deliberate detour.

mechanics.text: The trail uses a fruit-heavy bush mix and adds one large forest-bear encounter where a legal seat exists.
Berry-runts may also lurk behind the first bush row; fruit picking and thorn contact use the shared rules.
Let the bear visibly investigate a nearby berry bush while idle, explaining its presence before combat.

loop: Spot the bear → choose a safe approach → take nearby fruit or pass by.

feeling: A playful sequence of small breaks and occasional rewards.
arrival: Terracotta and tan pots appear on the road and in two verge rows, giving the route an immediately readable interaction.
art: Keep the existing pots in exactly terracotta #bf6f4a and tan #c29c67.
Use intact and smashed pot frames to show where the player has already searched.
Let the warm road palette support the pots without introducing more decorative colours.

mechanics.text: Pots can be smashed; most are empty, with coins and occasional existing item rewards in the shared pot loot table.
Road pots and two verge rows create repeated optional stops; occupied seats leave gaps.
Vary the existing ceramic break sound by pot size so a run of pots has a tactile rhythm.

loop: Choose a pot → smash → inspect the result → follow the next intact group.

feeling: Useful supplies are close at hand, but someone is already scavenging them.
arrival: Rows of barrels make the rewards obvious; pairs of goblin grunts turn browsing into a tactical choice.
art: Use existing wooden barrels and their broken states as the route's main visual rhythm.
Keep hanging lantern posts and warm light around the barrel rows.
Leave readable gaps between barrels so both members of a grunt pair can be spotted.

mechanics.text: Barrels use existing container loot and smashing interactions.
Eligible roadside posts can hold two goblin grunts, with gaps between encounters.
Give idle grunts a short barrel-inspection animation, making guarded supplies legible before they notice the player.

loop: Scan a barrel group → assess its guards → fight or bypass → collect supplies.

feeling: A practical gathering route where useful stone is always underfoot.
arrival: Common rocks, flint and rubble extend onto the route itself and stop at the first verge row.
art: Use only the existing common-rock, flint and rubble forms; omit outer decorative rock types.
Keep the grey road surface restrained so loose harvestable pieces remain distinct.
Preserve clear space beyond the first verge row rather than filling the scene with boulders.

mechanics.text: Common mineral rocks use normal tier-one mining; flint and rubble retain their ordinary gathering interactions.
Finds can occupy the road and first verge row; blocked seats do not push them farther outward.
Use distinct existing impact sounds for mining rock and picking loose flint, reinforcing the two gathering actions.

loop: Spot a useful piece → pick or mine → move to the next find.

feeling: A soft, low-pressure stretch where a small discovery can interrupt an easy walk.
arrival: Long grass spreads across the road and two verge rows, with no added ferns or shrubs competing for attention.
art: Use only the existing long-grass sprite for added vegetation.
Keep grass-coloured terrain and subdued paving visible beneath the tufts.
Let cleared grass leave an obvious local opening without adding flowers or new props.

mechanics.text: Long grass is harvestable using the shared clearing interaction.
Individual grass plants have the existing rare coin and egg finds.
Add a quiet grass-brushing footstep layer while crossing uncleared tufts, fading it on cleared cells.

loop: Walk through grass → clear an inviting patch → inspect any small find → move on.

feeling: A sheltered timber-and-forage corridor beneath mature trees.
arrival: Mature trunks establish the enclosure; small mushrooms punctuate an otherwise uncluttered forest floor.
art: Keep the existing mature-tree silhouettes and forest ground treatment.
Use small mushroom art as a close-range reward cue beside the trunks.
Do not generate stumps or bushes; preserve open ground between the mature trees.

mechanics.text: Generated mature trees use normal tree chopping and timber rewards.
Small mushrooms are pickable, while the existing medium mushroom clusters yield wood and mushroom when chopped.
Lower ambient wind and add a subdued canopy sound on entry, making the enclosure perceptible without extra props.

loop: Enter the shade → inspect the tree line → forage or chop → return to the path.

feeling: An uneasy passage where familiar gathering cues sit among signs of death.
arrival: Dead trees, brown soil and headstones replace the living forest, with mushrooms close to the dark road.
art: Use the existing dead-tree art, headstones and dark road palette.
Keep the brown-soil ground distinct from the green forest routes.
Leave mushrooms visible near the headstones rather than obscuring them with extra decoration.

mechanics.text: The route is marked as a haunting habitat and participates in the shared haunting rules.
Dead-tree finds and mushrooms retain ordinary chopping and picking interactions.
Introduce a brief distant rustle at the first headstone, without adding an enemy or implying a guaranteed ambush.

loop: Read the changed ground → watch the gaps between dead trees → gather cautiously or keep moving.

feeling: A compact scavenging sampler that keeps changing what catches your eye.
arrival: Plants, pots, barrels and stones share the road and verges, with occasional crop plants and distinctive ore colours.
art: Use existing mature T1–T2 crop art for potato, cress, onion and nut plants, alongside ordinary finds.
Let existing copper and pale pink rose-quartz rock art provide occasional colour accents.
Add no trees; retain only the styling of satellite-detected trees already present.

mechanics.text: The seeded mix includes common plants and containers, occasional native crop plants, and copper or rose-quartz deposits.
Each find keeps its normal picking, chopping, smashing or mining interaction; the crop plants are harvestable wild plants, not timed farm plots.
Briefly name a newly encountered find on approach, encouraging players to learn the different interactions without creating a collection quest.

loop: Notice an unfamiliar find → identify its action → gather → look for a different kind.

feeling: A dependable dry crossing through a visibly wet landscape.
arrival: Pools appear on both sides while the road and crossings remain continuous and completely dry.
art: Use existing water tiles on both verges and retain a crisp dry road boundary.
Keep road lamps readable above the water without adding another deck or bridge asset.
Preserve dry intersecting roads so the route never appears flooded.

mechanics.text: The terrain pass creates water pools beside the road, up to three cells outward.
Road footprints and crossings are excluded from those pools, preserving the dry route.
Add a quiet shoreline sound near the verge pools that fades at the centre of the road, reinforcing the safe crossing.

loop: Notice water flanking the road → follow the dry crossing → emerge onto ordinary ground.
